note: The stem asks for the one option that is not, cannot or does not (não é cinegética, não pode utilizar, não constitui crime), or for the wrong statement (incorreta, errada); read past the não and the two true options look right. Tag when não negates the stem's verb or the stem asks for the wrong one; not for a não inside a term that only names the ground (terrenos não ordenados, terrenos não cinegéticos), which the peek translates.

só and apenas, like unicamente and a única, limit what follows to that and nothing else (só às narcejas, apenas é válida para algumas espécies). Tag when the answer turns on the limit: an option with só set against a wider one (só em zonas de caça against em todos os locais), or a stem that asks for the one case (só é eficaz … em que situação).

desde que attaches a condition, with the verb in the present subjunctive (desde que estejam, desde que tenha): the rule holds only when the condition is met. Tag when the answer turns on whether that condition makes the option true, typically a 'permitida, desde que …' or 'Sim, desde que …' option set against a flat ban; not when a number or a name decides and the condition is incidental.

bem como adds a second item to the same rule, so 'proibido caçar nos povoados, bem como numa faixa de proteção' bans the strip too; it is never a contrast or 'well, as'. Tag when the answer turns on what the bem como clause extends the rule to (which places carry the strip, whether the strip is covered); not when the strip's width is the whole question.

An absolute (é sempre proibido, nunca, ninguém, em nenhuma situação, em todos os locais, qualquer espécie) claims a rule holds without exception, against options that make it conditional or partial. Tag when the answer turns on whether the absolute holds: the absolute is keyed (no one is exempt) or it is the distractor beside a conditional keyed option (só quando sinalizados).

tanto X como Y and quer X quer Y mean 'both X and Y' (quer here is not 'wants'), and ambos os sexos is 'both sexes'. Tag when the options set one against both (the female alone, the male alone, both sexes; by day, by night, either) and the answer turns on which.

mais X que and menos X que compare two things, often two at once (cabeça mais forte e menos afilada; mais pesado e menos vivo), and each distractor flips one direction. Tag when the answer turns on the direction of a comparison, or of a superlative in the stem (distribuição menos alargada); not when the options differ in a noun or a number.

pouco before an adjective turns it down to 'not very', nearly its opposite (pouco sociável, vegetação pouco densa, pouco variada), never 'a little'; set beside bastante, muito or the bare adjective (densa), it flips what the option says. Tag when the answer turns on pouco: the keyed option against muito or bastante, or a distractor false only because of pouco (pouco importante, pouco densa); not when another fact in the option decides (uma zona pouca protegida).

en: Above or below a limit (superior a, inferior a)
note: superior a and inferior a mean above and below a figure, never better or worse; a mais de and a menos de 100 metros mean beyond and within 100 metres. Tag when the answer turns on which side of the limit applies (a blood alcohol rate inferior a 1,2 g/l is no crime); not when the options differ only in the number.

The options place the same event before, during or after another (caem durante a época do cio, depois da época do cio; só enquanto dura o incêndio, e durante os 30 dias seguintes). Tag when the answer turns on that time relation; not when the options differ only in a date, a month or a number.

pt: sem consentimento de quem de direito
note: 'Proibido caçar sem consentimento de quem de direito' bans hunting only without the consent of the person entitled, so with that consent it is allowed. Tag when the answer turns on consent: a ban that consent lifts set against a flat ban (nunca pode caçar, sempre proibido) or against someone else's permission (the junta de freguesia).

The stem states a rule and asks for the one case it leaves out (exceto; há um que não pode; há um deles que carece). Tag when the answer is that exception; a stem that asks it with não also takes negative-stem.

en: What it is called (dá-se o nome de, designa-se)
note: The stem asks for a Portuguese name or for what a name denotes; dá-se o nome de X a Y reads 'Y is called X', so check which side the stem gives (dá-se o nome de navalhas aos dentes asks which teeth). Tag every question that asks for a name or its meaning; the name under test is never glossed in a language note.

The options are three whole statements, often about different facts, and the stem gives no context, so each must be read and judged on its own. Tag every question whose stem asks which statement (frase, afirmação, regra) is correct or wrong; the wrong-one form takes negative-stem too.

en: Yes or no, with a reason
note: The options answer yes or no and add a reason or a condition (Não, porque …; Sim, mas só …; Sim, desde que …), and at least two share the same yes or no. Tag when the answer turns on the reason or the condition rather than on the yes or no alone.

The stem sets out one hunter's situation (month, ground, method, quarry, number of dogs) and asks whether it is lawful, which licence it needs or which infraction it commits; several details are given and only one or two decide. Tag when the answer turns on spotting which detail of the case matters.

Each option lists several species, places, days or methods, and a list is right only if every item in it is; a distractor usually shares all but one item with the keyed list (Patos, galinha-d’água e galeirão; Patos, galinhola e galeirão). Tag when the answer turns on the item that differs.
